original_question: Is an arbitrary product of strong d-spaces again a strong d-space? Here a T0 space X is strong d if for every directed set D, point x, and open set U, whenever intersection_{d in D} (up d intersect up x) is contained in U, one already has up d intersect up x contained in U for some d in D.
target_in_paper: Section 8, Question 8.10: "Is the product space of an arbitrary family of strong d-spaces again a strong d-space?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact open problem. It correctly identifies that the target is closure of strong d-spaces under arbitrary products, and it reproduces the defining condition of a strong d-space essentially as in Definition 8.1. It also correctly keeps the T0 hypothesis and quantifies over directed sets, points, and open sets.
missing_details: The paper phrases the problem for a family {X_i}_{i in I} of T0 spaces and asks about the topological product space \prod_{i in I} X_i with the product topology.

The directed set D is a nonempty directed subset of X with respect to the specialization order, since throughout the paper a T0 space is viewed as a poset via its specialization order unless stated otherwise.
The notation \uparrow d and \uparrow x refers to principal upper sets in that specialization order.

The nearby context shows that Proposition 8.9 proves the reverse implication: if \prod_{i in I} X_i is a strong d-space, then each factor X_j is a strong d-space because each factor is a retract of the product. So the open question is specifically the converse closure-under-products direction.
For complete stand-alone phrasing, it helps to say explicitly that every factor is assumed to satisfy Definition 8.1, rather than only naming them 'strong d-spaces'.
refined_question: Let {X_i}_{i\in I} be a family of T0 spaces, each regarded with its specialization order, and suppose that each X_i is a strong d-space in the sense that for every nonempty directed subset D\subseteq X_i, every x\in X_i, and every open set U\subseteq X_i, if \bigcap_{d\in D}(\uparrow d\cap\uparrow x)\subseteq U, then \uparrow d\cap\uparrow x\subseteq U for some d\in D. Must the product space \prod_{i\in I} X_i, equipped with the product topology, also be a strong d-space?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 8 on strong d-spaces rather than the introductory problems from another part of the paper. The exact official target is Question 8.10. Definition 8.1 supplies the hidden conventions needed to make the question stand-alone: strong d-spaces are T0 spaces, D ranges over directed subsets with respect to the specialization order, and \uparrow is taken in that order. The immediately preceding Proposition 8.9 explains why the paper asks only the converse direction: each factor of a strong-d product is automatically strong d because it is a retract of the product. Proposition 8.5 and Lemma 8.7 give nearby structural criteria for strong d-spaces, but they do not replace Question 8.10 with a broader or different problem. No algebraic ambient data, degree restrictions, or asymptotic quantifiers are relevant here.
